key_insight: Topology-guided flow targets combined with a DMDc reduced-order model and model predictive control reduce mean drag while retaining the main vortices.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a computationally compact strategy for active aerodynamic flow control around an oscillating wing.
method: Detect and characterize vortices using persistence diagrams of absolute vorticity.
Compute a target flow offline by gradient descent in reduced space, retaining useful vortices.
Track the target with DMDc-based receding-horizon MPC solved as a small-dimensional convex quadratic program.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests around an oscillating aircraft wing at seven vibration frequencies report reduced mean drag coefficient while preserving the main vortices.
watch_item: Evidence is numerical; robustness to experimental noise and operating conditions beyond the tested frequencies remains unestablished.
paper_title: Active flow control based on topological data analysis and a DMDc reduced-order model for drag reduction
